questions.note: Order holds in scope: the hallux is longest, toe 2 shorter, the 1–2 gap open. Shaping is weak: in profile the hallux tapers to a pointed wedge, about 14–15 mm thick at the nail root, and from below it is a squared block; toe 2 is an even tube with no PIP swelling or waist; the knuckle wrinkles on both are evenly spaced stamped grooves.

Both plates sit in folds, show free-edge thickness and are trimmed straight, but the hallux nail reads as a flat press-on tile with a French-tip band and no crescent lunula (a straight white rim instead), and both its distal corners are torn; toe 2's plate is combed with bold white streaks and sits in a square-cut slot.

Extensor ridges run down the dorsum toward the hallux and toe 2 as soft relief that catches the light in the top34 views, not painted lines. But there are no veins at all at the toe bases or on the forefoot, where the anchors' lean feet show a clear network, and a scar-like groove crosses the EHL over the first MTP. The saphenous vein is out of these views.

Declared first pass, scored as seen. Shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows. The micro-relief is wrong in kind: pad ridges are straight stripes at one angle across every toe, with no whorl or loop; the dorsal crackle is coarse, dark-lined crazing that even shows under toe 2's plate; broad oily highlights and one even, young pink read waxy.

defects.what: In profile the hallux thins to a pointed wedge: the nail's free edge is the foremost point with no pulp ahead of or below it, and the toe is about 14–15 mm thick at the nail root (spec 19) and 20–21 mm at the IP (Jeff's direction about 25).
defects.fix: Thicken the distal phalanx so the dorsum over the nail runs nearly level and the pulp forms a blunt dome reaching as far forward as the free edge and rounding down to the floor, as in the anchor photos.

defects.what: From below, the hallux pad is a rectangular block with straight parallel sides and a squared-off end, and toe 2's pad is the same in miniature; neither pulp bulges or rounds into its tip.
defects.fix: Real toe pulps are oval, fleshy domes, widest mid-pad and rounding into the tip; the hallux pad is broad and bulbous, pinched into a waist at the IP crease.

defects.what: The hallux nail reads as a press-on: a flat, evenly lit rounded-square tile with a straight proximal edge, tight proximal corners and a bright, even white French-tip band.
defects.fix: A real big-toe plate is clearly convex (about 11 mm radius) and darkens toward its sides, meets a curved cuticle line with no proximal corners, and ends in an ivory free edge of slightly uneven width with a faint grey line beneath.

defects.what: Torn geometry at the hallux nail's medial distal corner: a dark cluster of jagged spikes where the plate's corner meets the fold, spiky in clay too and visible as dark specks at native size in the front and top34 views.
defects.fix: The medial nail fold should taper smoothly into the hyponychium under the free-edge corner, the plate passing cleanly beside or under the fold skin, never through it.

defects.what: The same tear at the hallux nail's lateral distal corner: a white saw-tooth zigzag, regular as a zip, runs along the fold edge beside the free edge; spiky in clay too.
defects.fix: A smooth lateral sulcus ending cleanly under the free-edge corner, with no intersection between the plate and the fold.

defects.what: Deep in the 1–2 web, on the hallux's lateral wall, the surface is crumpled and torn: jagged spikes in clay and a black ragged slit in the eval render; crinkles also show in the front and top34 clay views.
defects.fix: A real 1–2 web is a smooth U-shaped skin fold with a soft shadow gradient into the cleft, with no self-intersection.

defects.what: No crescent lunula on the hallux: the plate's proximal end is a straight, full-width, glossy white band with a hard lower edge, reading as the exposed rim of a stuck-on plate.
defects.fix: A soft, milky crescent, convex distally and about 3.5 mm deep at the centre, fading toward the lateral folds and partly hidden under a skin-coloured cuticle.

defects.what: Toe 2 is an even tube from the PIP to the pulp: straight parallel sides, no knuckle swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx, and four evenly spaced stamped grooves over the PIP.
defects.fix: A real second toe swells at the PIP knuckle, narrows over the middle phalanx and widens again at the pulp; its dorsal wrinkles are a loose, irregular cluster of fine lines.

defects.what: Toe 2's nail plate is combed with bold, high-contrast white longitudinal streaks over its whole width, like brushed aluminium or glass fibre.
defects.fix: Real longitudinal ridging is about 0.01 mm deep and shows only as a faint ripple in the highlight; the plate reads smooth, pink over the bed and slightly milky.

defects.what: No hair: the hallux's proximal phalanx has no tuft and toe 2 none of its few hairs, so the toes read hairless and young beside the anchor photos.
defects.fix: 8–12 dark hairs 5–8 mm long lying flat toward the tip on the hallux's proximal phalanx, and 2–4 short hairs on toe 2's.

defects.what: A single long, thin, glossy groove crosses the dorsum over the first MTP and reads as a healed cut or scar, not a skin fold.
defects.fix: At rest the skin over the first MTP is smooth or carries a few short, soft transverse wrinkles that fade out at the sides.

defects.what: The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced, parallel smooth grooves, like one sculpted stroke repeated.
defects.fix: Real dorsal IP skin carries a lozenge-shaped cluster of many fine, broken wrinkles of unequal length and depth over slightly loose skin.

defects.what: A straight, hard-edged step runs across toe 2's plantar surface below its proximal crease: a seam with a shading break and white specks at its lateral end, unlike any flexion crease.
defects.fix: Plantar digital creases are soft, curved folds at the joints; the skin between them is continuous.

defects.what: Toe 2's lateral nail folds stop in square-cut walls at the free-edge corners, leaving dark rectangular slots, and the free edge has a small V-kink at its centre.
defects.fix: The lateral folds taper smoothly toward the tip and the free edge rides just beyond the hyponychium, with no pocket around it.

defects.what: Under the hallux free edge the hyponychium is rippled like crumpled film, and a second rolled lip runs parallel below the free edge.
defects.fix: The hyponychium is a smooth, slightly recessed band of skin under the free edge that merges into the pulp.

defects.what: A small blister-like lump sits on the hallux's proximal nail fold, left of centre toward the medial corner (also in the front and top34 clay views).
defects.fix: The eponychium is an even, thin roll of skin along the whole cuticle line.

defects.what: At the plantar apex of the 1–2 web, stacked ripple lines and a jagged fleck mark a mesh fault where the hallux's pad meets the web.
defects.fix: From below, the web apex is a smooth, soft fold between the two pads.

ranked: [D1] In profile the hallux is a thin wedge ending in a point at the nail's free edge, about 14–15 mm thick at the nail root. A real big toe ends in a blunt, domed pulp that bulges forward and down under the nail; this one reads like a beak.
[D2] From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rectangular blocks with straight sides and squared ends; real pulps are oval, fleshy domes, widest mid-pad and rounding into the tip.

[D3] The hallux nail is a press-on: a flat rounded-square tile with a straight proximal edge, tight corners and a bright, even French tip. A real big-toe nail is convex, meets a curved cuticle line and ends in an ivory, slightly uneven free edge.

[D4] [D5] Both distal corners of the hallux nail are torn, a dark spiky cluster medially and a white saw-tooth zigzag laterally, spiky in clay too and already visible as dark specks at the nail corners in the front and top34 views.
[D6] The 1–2 web is torn deep on the hallux's lateral wall: a black, ragged slit in the toe 2 closeup and crumpled spikes in clay, where a real web is a smooth U-fold with a soft shadow.

[D7] No lunula on the hallux: the proximal end of the plate is a straight, full-width, glossy white band with a hard edge, reading as the rim of a stuck-on plate rather than a milky crescent under the cuticle.
[D8] Toe 2 is an even tube from knuckle to pulp, with no PIP swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx and four evenly spaced stamped rings: a sausage toe with grooves rather than a jointed one.
[D9] Toe 2's nail is combed with bold white longitudinal streaks across the whole plate, like brushed metal; real ridging shows only as a faint ripple in the highlight.

Declared first-pass skin material, but it distorts the scope: the pads' friction ridges are straight stripes at one angle across every toe and across the IP crease, with no whorl or loop, so the pulps read as corduroy.

Also the declared material: the dorsal crackle is coarse, dark-lined crazing like cracked glaze, even over the toes, nail folds, hyponychium and pulp tips, and it shows through toe 2's plate on the nail bed.

The toes read young and clean: one even pink-beige, a wet, oily sheen on the dorsum, no redness over the knuckles, no dryness at the tips or nail folds. Mostly the declared material, but it makes the scope a foot model's, not a 40-year-old soldier's.
[D10] No hair: no tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2. The hairier anchor feet carry dark hairs there; bald toes read young and mannequin-like.
No veins at the toe bases or on the forefoot: the anchors' lean male feet show a dorsal venous network running toward the webs; here only the extensor ridges give the dorsum any relief.
[D11] A long, thin, glossy groove across the first MTP's dorsum reads as a healed cut or scar; real skin there is smooth or carries a few short, soft wrinkles that fade at the sides.
[D12] The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced parallel grooves, like one sculpted stroke repeated; real knuckle skin has a loose cluster of fine, broken, unequal lines.
[D13] A straight, hard-edged step runs across toe 2's plantar surface, a seam with a shading break and white specks, unlike any flexion crease.
[D14] Toe 2's lateral folds end in square-cut walls at the free-edge corners, leaving dark slots, and its free edge has a V-kink: the nail sits in a machined pocket.
[D15] Under the hallux free edge the hyponychium is rippled like crumpled film, with a second rolled lip below the free edge.
[D16] A small blister-like lump sits on the hallux's proximal nail fold, left of centre.
[D17] A jagged fleck and stacked ripple lines at the plantar apex of the 1–2 web.
